A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, despite the changed title and terminology. All pages, equations, figures, tables, and end matter support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original SNN experiments on working-memory copying and six simulated control environments, including component ablations, generalization, and neural-damage tests.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes in Table 1 and Figures 2–6.

M1.justification: The explicit plasticity update in Eq. 1, LIF dynamics, network architecture, and PEPG Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. LP/HP become SCP/PDP. The new presynaptic wording conflicts with the retained equation rather than establishing a revised computational procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain the copying task and ant_dir, swimmer_dir, halfcheetah_vel, hopper_vel, fetch, and ur5e environments. Coverage of unseen targets, changing-direction trajectories, and temporary/permanent neural injury is also unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain direct weight optimization, random-action chance performance, and the same plasticity-component variants. Table 1 and Figure 3C rename LP/HP variants as SCP/PDP without adding or removing comparators.

E3.justification: The reported protocols remain the same, including 128 hidden neurons for control tasks, eight training and 72 generalization directions/speeds, and the copying-task reward and accuracy definitions. Tables 2–3 retain the neuron settings and training budget of 1500 generations with 128 offspring.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablations, membrane-reset memory analysis, synaptic-weight visualizations, temporary/permanent damage tests, neuronal-state embeddings, and changing-target trajectory demonstrations. No substantive analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 1 reports means and standard deviations over five trials in both versions. Figure uncertainty displays are retained, with no new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 values and the findings displayed in Figures 2–6 are unchanged after matching renamed variants. For example, ant_dir remains 6904±801 for full plasticity and 1069±98 for direct weight training. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the mathematical content of Algorithm 1 are retained. The new attribution to a parametric expansion of the Spiking BCM rule supplies conceptual grounding, without adding a derivation, formal property, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The stated conceptual contribution shifts from unifying learning and homeostatic plasticity to abstract, parametric modeling through PDLF. The central claim of learning plasticity rules instead of fixed weights, and the claimed memory, multitasking, generalization, and robustness benefits, remain.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 replaces the detailed homeostatic interpretation with SCP/PDP explanations. It now describes B_ij x_j+D_ij as presynaptic-dependent, whereas v1 correctly describes its postsynaptic dependence and both versions define x_j as postsynaptic. The subsequent interpretations of experimental results and applicability remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Data Availability paragraph stating that code and data have been deposited in a PDLF GitHub repository, providing access information absent from v1. Existing implementation settings and optimizer details remain unchanged; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially revises positioning from biological metaplasticity and LP/HP coordination toward parametric abstraction and Spiking BCM. Much homeostatic, metaplasticity, and neuronal-heterogeneity coverage disappears, including discussion of Meta-spikepropamine and Synaptic motor adaptation. New references support BCM-related modeling and backpropagation's biological plausibility, including Bekolay et al. and Lillicrap et al.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and Section 2.1 are substantially rewritten, with shorter mechanism and evolutionary-strategy explanations. Terminology changes throughout the document, although the overall Results–Discussion–Method organization and most experimental prose remain.

P2.justification: Figure 1 removes the two upper LP/HP explanatory panels and revises component labels. Figure 3C legends and Table 1 row labels adopt SCP/PDP terminology. Existing figures, tables, and Algorithm 1 shift position with the text; the experimental displays otherwise remain.

improvement.justification: The new code/data pointer and explicit BCM connection improve documentation, but Section 2.1 introduces a presynaptic/postsynaptic contradiction absent from v1's explanation of Eq. 1. The revision also removes explicit positioning against previously discussed learned-plasticity SNN methods. These losses modestly outweigh the documentation gains, weakening explanatory accuracy and contextual completeness while leaving the experimental evidence unchanged.
